expectations.text: Identifies Ferrolane's complete lack of a public API as the exception to the defensive-positioning framing, making MCP a genuinely new acquisition channel rather than a defensive duplicate.
expectations.evidence: "MCP is the first machine-readable interface they ever shipped, which makes it a possible new acquisition channel"

expectations.text: Cites that roughly half the companies shipping MCP servers had no public REST API.
expectations.evidence: "Roughly half of companies shipping MCP servers had no public REST API."

expectations.text: Separates the competitor announcement from real demand, and asks for demand evidence - buyer RFPs, security questionnaires, customer requests, or an existing community-built server - before sizing the build.
expectations.evidence: "two competitors announcing MCP servers is not demand evidence"; asks sales for RFPs

expectations.text: Flags that with no machine-readable interface at all the tool surface cannot be derived from an existing contract, which changes the effort and ROI framing.
expectations.evidence: "there is no stable contract to derive tools from"

expectations.text: Budgets honestly: demo-grade in days versus production-grade in months plus standing maintenance, citing an order of 150-250 hours for a simple hand-built API-integration server.
expectations.evidence: "A demo server takes a weekend. A production server takes months plus a standing maintenance commitment... 150-250 hour"

expectations.text: Names the park rule: if tool-call volume stays flat and no RFP demand materializes after two full quarters, keep it as low-maintenance table stakes and explicitly defer the production build.
expectations.evidence: "If two full quarters pass with flat usage and no RFP demand, park it at stage 1"

expectations.text: Names the accelerate override: a hard MCP requirement in actual buyer RFPs justifies skipping past the staged timeline.
expectations.evidence: "if MCP is a hard requirement in real RFPs, accelerate"

expectations.text: Sequences a read-only launch first rather than shipping write tools in the first release.
expectations.evidence: "Writes by January are not realistic and not safe"; stage 1 read-only

expectations.text: Asks about the effort ceiling and the date the server must land by - engineering hours, maintenance appetite, reversibility - before recommending a hosting posture.
expectations.evidence: "What is your engineering ceiling in hours"; "Is January a procurement deadline or a competitive-optics date?"
